correctness.rationale: The discrete Fourier eigenvalues n*sum_h exp(-t(r+nh)^2) are strictly positive. Poisson summation and the Jacobi triple product factor their inverse multiplier into summable reciprocal (1+a z)(1+a z^-1) factors with 0<a<1. Their even-2n-cycle inverse coefficients are exactly (-1)^j(a^j+a^(2n-j))/((1-a^2)(1-a^(2n))), with strictly positive, strictly radially decreasing twisted amplitudes; the centered cyclic-ball intersection formula proves monotonicity is preserved under convolution and a finite strict prefix plus the l1-small infinite tail keeps strictness. Folding from 2n to n gives (-1)^j(a_j+(-1)^n a_(n-j)), which has precisely the shorter-distance parity even on odd n. Boundary n=2 and the antipodal distance are included. This is an analytic argument for every real t, not an inference from numerical logs. Independent 240-digit Fourier-inversion checks across n=2..12, t in {0.1,0.5,2,5,10} corroborated all 55 matrices; precision must be high because extreme t is ill-conditioned.
